title: Record or reject the 1280px rail break?
context:
Goal: A session that builds or tests the shell reads the right screen widths.
Problem (rule): The shell sets its default side rail break at 1280px (app/src/App.css:23), and no record says so. The records you ruled (D95, shell rail and palette sheet; D276, palette go-to lists screens) give 1024 and 640. Only the code holds the 1280 now, and a record change needs your word.
Based on (read): banchi app/src/App.css:23 sets --bn-rail-break-px to 1280; a search of docs/ finds no rail-break text (main 0657163).
Departs from: D95 says nothing about a 1280 rail break and the code uses it — D95 gets an AMENDED line that records 1280 as the default break.

options.label: Record 1280 in D95
options.how: Add an AMENDED line to D95 that names the 1280 default rail break.
options.gain: The records match the screen; a session reads one width.
options.lose: A width nobody ruled becomes a ruling.

options.label: Call 1280 wrong
options.how: Rule 1280 a defect and change the code to the recorded widths.
options.gain: The shell follows the widths you ruled.
options.lose: A code change on a screen, with a screen check, and a layout shift at 1024 to 1279.

title: Delete the old publish routes or record them?
home: banchi D273 (one press sends listings live)
context:
Goal: No price change reaches buyers without a live read first.
Problem (money): D273 (one press sends listings live) says the one press is the only route that publishes. Two older routes, /push and /publish, still move an upload live with only a confirm and no live reconcile. A price change can go live through them, so it needs your word.
Based on (read): banchi server/capture_server.py:780-781 route both paths; pipeline_routes.py do_markdown_publish calls move_to_live (main 0657163).
Based on (notes): Whether any script still calls them is unmeasured; the web app no longer calls publishMarkdown.
Departs from: D273 says one route publishes and the code has three — both old routes are deleted, or recorded as a second door with a live reconcile.

options.label: Delete both routes
options.how: Remove /push and /publish and their handlers in a lane.
options.gain: One door to the live price; D273 is true.
options.lose: Any script that uses them breaks; unmeasured.

options.label: Keep as second door
options.how: Record them in D273 and add the live reconcile to each.
options.gain: No caller breaks.
options.lose: Two doors to guard; more code to keep right.

title: Add numbered-box exceptions or fix the screens?
context:
Goal: You read every box by its name, never a number.
Problem (rule): D259 (boxes show names only) says a box is shown only by its name, everywhere. Home, the capture screen, a CLI refusal and the Codes screen still draw 'Box N' or 'Slot N'. D259 lists two exceptions only, and its check does not scan screen text, so nothing catches these.
Based on (read): banchi app/src/Home.tsx:405, CaptureScreen.tsx:4555 and cli/cmd_emit.py:263-275 draw box numbers (main 0657163).
Based on (read): D259 line 60 lists only two numbered refusals as exceptions.
Departs from: D259 shows boxes only by name and four places show numbers — those four places are named as exceptions, or fixed to names.

options.label: Name the exceptions
options.how: Add these four places to D259 as named exceptions.
options.gain: No screen work; records match the screens.
options.lose: The box number stays visible where you ruled it hidden.

options.label: Fix the screens
options.how: A lane changes each place to show the name, and the check learns to scan screen text.
options.gain: The rule holds everywhere.
options.lose: Four screen changes and a screen check.

title: Allow the Difference row or remove it?

context:
Goal: A sale shows no misleading verdict.
Problem (rule): D227 (product history is its own route) says it computes no comparison of a fill against its bucket. The product history screen draws a 'What You Got' block with a Difference row. No decision covers the block, and only the code protects the rule now.

Based on (read): Debt 070 calls the panel a read-only diagnostic and does not rule on it.

options.label: Allow the plain number
options.how: Amend D227 to allow the Difference row as a plain number with no verdict.
options.gain: You keep the figure; the record is true.
options.lose: A comparison, which D227 kept out, is now allowed.

options.label: Remove the row
options.how: A lane deletes the Difference row.
options.gain: D227 stays as ruled; no verdict can mislead.

title: Reopen D39 or retire it?
home: banchi D39 (run scope is the handed selection)
context:
Goal: The record for starting a run matches how a run starts.
Problem (rule): D39 (run scope is the handed selection) says the source control writes the selection on every press, and says to reopen it if no run starts from a ticked selection. The writer was retired on your word and nothing writes the handoff now. Whether any path still starts a run from ticked cards is unmeasured.
Based on (read): banchi app/src/runHandoff.ts:152-160 says carryScope was retired; only readers remain (main 0657163).
Based on (notes): D180 says a press takes one selection; that no ticked-card run path remains is unmeasured.
Departs from: D39 says a press writes the handoff and nothing does — D39 is reopened and rewritten, or retired.

options.label: Reopen and rewrite D39
options.how: Rewrite D39 to say what the readers do now.
options.gain: The record states how a run really starts.
options.lose: More record work than a retire.

options.label: Retire D39
options.how: Mark D39 retired and point to the record that replaced it.
options.gain: A stale rule leaves the set.
options.lose: Any ticked-card run path that does exist loses its rule.

title: Make D269's closed disclosure the rule everywhere?

context:

Problem (rule): D210 (rescue is press in words) says raw machine text is never visible, not even behind a disclosure. D269 (machine words in disclosure) later adopted a closed 'What the server said' disclosure as the rule, and amended only D196. D210 and three code comments still repeat the flat rule.

options.label: D269 shape is the rule

options.lose: Machine words stay one click away.

options.lose: The disclosure stops helping when something fails.

context:
Goal: No record tells a session to mint a credential the app ignores, and you can still recover the ledger from a backup.
Problem (rule): About fifteen records and CLAUDE.md still tell a reader to put a GitHub token on each device. The app no longer writes to GitHub and no device holds a token. Retiring them needs a ruling on one form: a dated Retired line, or none.

title: Keep the app iPhone-only and open a Mac debt?
context:
Goal: The app you expect to ship is the one the records promise.
Problem (goal): native-swift-rebuild rejects Swift on the iPhone only and promises one SwiftUI target for iOS and macOS. The project builds iOS only. Two later records call iPhone-only a default that swift-rebuild supports, which it does not. You rejected iPhone-only, so only you can reverse it.
Based on (read): mailaudit docs/decisions/native-swift-rebuild.md:80 and native/project.yml (TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY 1, iOS only) (main cd3e12f).
Based on (notes): No owner ruling reverses the rejection and no debt names the Mac app.
Departs from: native-swift-rebuild rejects iPhone-only and the build is iPhone-only — the record is rewritten to say iPhone-only ships and a debt names the Mac target.

options.label: Keep iPhone-only
options.how: Rewrite swift-rebuild in place to say iPhone-only, and open a debt for the Mac target.
options.gain: The record matches what ships.
options.lose: The Mac app you ruled for is pushed to a debt.

options.gain: The Mac app ships as ruled.
options.lose: More native work; the records stay wrong until it lands.

why: Recommended in the audit report: only the iPhone app ships today.

context:
Goal: An undo stays reachable when the ledger is empty.
Problem (rule): recent-checks-can-be-undone says the Recent cell shows only when the ledger holds data, as Reset does. Reset shows on every ledger, so the cell would hide right after a Reset empties it. The same record states a paper fill as settled, and another record calls it an unbuilt default.
Based on (read): mailaudit src/app.jsx:6573-6576 says Reset shows on an empty ledger; recent-checks-can-be-undone.md:145 (main cd3e12f).
Based on (ruling): recovery-control-not-state-gated: a recovery control must not depend on the state it recovers.
Departs from: The Recent cell shows only when the ledger holds data — the record is rewritten so it shows on every ledger, and the paper fill is called an unbuilt default.

options.label: Show on every ledger
options.how: Rewrite :145 to show the cell always and :56 to call the fill unbuilt. No code moves.
options.gain: Undo stays reachable; the record matches Reset.
options.lose: The cell shows on an empty ledger, where it does nothing.
